title: Recognize response
description: Wire contract of the recognize capability's serve provider (SPEC 8.9.3): the JSON body that a served recognition backend returns with status 200 from POST /recognize. Last changed in spec version 0.102.0. The ingesting side applies SPEC 8.9.4 to every annotation itself and does not rely on this schema alone.

recognizer.description: Backend identity (SPEC 8.9.7): the model and model_version of the persisted recognition representation.

entities.description: Optional entity dictionary for the ids that annotations[].entities reference. The ingesting side keeps the entries that a persisted annotation references (SPEC 8.9.4). Ids SHOULD be stable across a corpus.

items.description: One recognized statement with a time span. The span maps directly to a persisted `time` citation, so it MUST satisfy 0 <= start_s <= end_s. A zero-length span (end_s == start_s) is permitted and denotes an instantaneous event (e.g. a single pitch-release frame). JSON Schema (2020-12) cannot express the cross-field `end_s >= start_s` bound portably, so the ingestion side DROPS a reversed span as a malformed annotation: the rest of the document's annotations proceed (SPEC 8.9.4); the per-field `minimum: 0` below is the portion the schema can enforce.

end_s.description: Span end in seconds (float). MUST be >= start_s; a reversed span is rejected at ingestion (see the item description).

event.description: Producer-defined event vocabulary (e.g. "pitch", "at_bat", "appearance"). Not enumerated by the contract.

entities.description: Entity ids involved; each should resolve in the top-level entities dictionary.

attributes.description: Optional flat producer-defined key/value scopes for this annotation (e.g. {"inning": "8", "half": "bottom"}; SPEC 9.10, Design 0006). Keys and values are opaque strings; the contract enumerates neither. Values are matched by literal equality, so the producer MUST emit each key's values in one canonical, documented form; the contract imposes no normalization. Keys with the dir2mcp: prefix are reserved for future core semantics and MUST NOT be emitted.

text.description: The human-readable statement. This is what gets chunked and indexed, so retrieval quality is bounded by its quality. MUST be non-empty and not whitespace-only (minLength + the `\S` pattern), so a blank statement can never enter the index as a non-searchable chunk.

confidence.description: Optional. Not persisted: the backend applies its own confidence floor before it answers (SPEC 8.9.3).

sources.description: Recognizer tags that contributed (e.g. "scorebug", "face"). Provenance metadata, not a relevance signal (df-005).

derivation.description: Optional. How this annotation came to exist. 'observed' means it is a reading of something recorded: a play-by-play feed entry, text read off an overlay, a matched face. 'generated' means a model DESCRIBED the media in its own words, so the annotation is an interpretation and not a record. Absent means observed. Any other value makes the annotation malformed, and the ingesting side drops it (SPEC 8.9.4). A consumer MUST NOT present a generated annotation as the source's own account of what happened (df-005).
